What a report on these filings would say, as data

Source: R/xbrl_report.R
xbrl_report_data.Rd

Runs the pipeline – standardise, screen, panel, ratios, robustness – on the filings given and gathers what a reader should know into one object: tables, and a short list of findings written out as sentences. It is the content of a report without its form, so that xbrl_report() can render it and anyone can build a report of their own from the same parts.

Usage

xbrl_report_data(
  x,
  cvr = NULL,
  type = NULL,
  peers = NULL,
  group = "class",
  lang = c("da", "en")
)

Arguments

x

A tibble from read_xbrl(), or from xbrl_validate() – which is the way to make several reports on the same filings without validating them for each.

cvr

CVR numbers to report on. NULL, the default, reports on every company in x.

type

"filing", "company", "cross_section" or "panel"; NULL decides from the data.

peers

A panel from xbrl_panel() to rank against, or NULL.

group

Columns that make companies comparable. Default "class"; see xbrl_ratios().

lang

"da" (default) or "en", for the sentences.

Value

A list of class cvrr_report_data: type, meta, highlights (character), and the tables the type has – for one company profile, figures, ratios, robustness, findings and technical; for many composition, distribution, robustness, vulnerable, findings and technical. panel is the robustness panel it was all read from.

Which report

The data decides, unless type does:

  • "filing" – one company, one year: who it is, its figures, what the checks and the auditor found, how robust it is.

  • "company" – one company over several years: the same, as a time series, and what changed since the year before.

  • "cross_section" – many companies, one year: what they look like together, how many show each sign of vulnerability, and which most.

  • "panel" – many companies over several years: the same, year by year.

Peers

A company's ratios mean more beside comparable companies'. Pass a panel of them as peers – the rest of a corpus, say – and each company is ranked among the companies of its group the same year. Without peers there is nothing to rank against, and the report says nothing about rank rather than rank a company against itself.

See also

xbrl_report() to render it, and xbrl_screen(), xbrl_panel(), xbrl_ratios(), xbrl_robustness() for the parts.

Other taxonomy: add_taxonomy(), check_breakdown(), check_cascade(), check_cashflow(), check_continuity(), check_inclusion(), check_movement(), check_statement(), read_taxonomy(), xbrl_accounts(), xbrl_company(), xbrl_fill(), xbrl_lines(), xbrl_movements(), xbrl_note_tables(), xbrl_panel(), xbrl_period(), xbrl_ratios(), xbrl_report(), xbrl_resolve(), xbrl_robustness(), xbrl_screen(), xbrl_standardise(), xbrl_validate()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
x <- read_xbrl("materiale/xbrl")
d <- xbrl_report_data(x, cvr = "12345678", peers = xbrl_panel(x))
d$highlights
xbrl_report(d, "12345678.html")

# the whole corpus
xbrl_report(xbrl_report_data(x), "corpus.html")
} # }
